title: Tata Capital Ltd - 544574 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Capital Q1 FY27 PAT rose 56% YoY to INR1,547 crore, with consolidated AUM up 22% YoY to INR2.91 lakh crore and credit cost at 1%.
summary.overview: Consolidated PAT of INR1,547 crore grew 56% YoY and 3% QoQ, with ROA at 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance) and ROE at 13.7%. AUM reached INR2.91 lakh crore, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, or 28% YoY excluding Motor Finance. Disbursements rose 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore, while the book grew about 10% YoY on a legacy run-off drag. Management announced the acquisition of Yogloans (gold loans), with RBI approval expected by calendar year-end, and raised USD400 million of international bonds, 4x oversubscribed.

segments.name: Housing Finance (Tata Capital Housing Finance)
segments.commentary: AUM INR89,416 crore, +24% YoY; PAT INR532 crore, +29% YoY; credit cost 0.05%, net NPA 0.3%, ROA 2.5%, ROE 18.4%. Cost-to-income about 30%; about 350 branches.

segments.name: Motor Finance
segments.commentary: Book moderated to INR24,445 crore as of June 2026 after a sequential decline; legacy net AUM run-off reduced to INR945 crore from INR3,139 crore a year earlier. Business remained profitable in Q1 FY27 despite seasonal credit cost rise.

segments.name: Unsecured Retail
segments.commentary: Unsecured retail disbursements up 50% YoY; unsecured retail AUM up 17% YoY. Management says the unsecured book will grow faster than overall book in FY27.

segments.name: Corporate and SME
segments.commentary: Retail plus SME is 85.4% of the portfolio, within the 85-88% target band; Corporate is the balance. Management says Corporate has 'maxed out' and will be syndicated down if originated above target.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance: ROA to rise from 2.3% to 2.6%, with two-thirds from margin expansion and one-third from opex leverage; management reiterated it is on track.
FY28 cost-to-income guided at 33-34%; a further 3-4 bps ROA gain from opex expected for the rest of FY27.
FY27 AUM growth guided at 23-25%; management said it is on track.
NIM expected to improve about 10 bps over FY27; cost of funds expected to rise about 8-10 bps on a daily-average basis this year.
Credit cost guidance of about 1% retained; management said any improvement beyond that is upside.
Consolidated debt-to-equity guided to about 6.2-6.3x; capital comfortable through June-September 2028 on current book-growth guidance; operates 200-250 bps above regulatory CET1 minimums.
Gold loans: expects approval by calendar year-end, about 500+ branches and INR4,000-5,000 crore portfolio over 2.5-3 years post-acquisition.
High-yield product contribution expected to increase by Q3 or Q4 FY27; book growth expected to converge toward disbursement growth over the next 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Yogloans acquisition: about 88.6% stake via capital infusion plus secondary purchase; pre-money equity valuation up to INR318 crore and INR93 crore primary infusion; 162 branches and AUM about INR708 crore as of March 2026; subject to RBI approval.
Network at 1,491 branches across 1,091 locations in 27 states and UTs, adding 14 branches in Q1; 8.8 million customers.
On-roll employee count 30,170, up about 5% YoY; incremental hiring focused on frontline sales and collections.
Micro Housing book about INR1,200 crore; plans to grow it about 100% in FY27 and 50-60% the following year. Combined Affordable and Micro Housing growth around 30%.
Housing listing: no decision yet; RBI upper-layer classification would give about three years to decide on listing.
demand_pricing: Disbursements up 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore; high-margin products account for 38% of disbursements, per management.
Management is repricing incremental lending to protect margins across Housing, Retail, SME and Corporate; no PLR hikes taken so far.
Management is conservative on commercial vehicles, construction equipment and petro-product-reliant MSMEs due to fuel-price pass-through risk; says no stress is visible in any segment.
Bounce rates improving month-on-month, including the current month, per management.
Motor Finance used-vehicle share held at 40-42% of disbursements; mix shifting toward ILMSCV from HCV, with yields raised in each segment.
Micro Housing ticket size about INR9 lakh versus INR15-16 lakh for Affordable Housing (per Q&A).

qa_highlights.question: Why does Corporate loan growth look fast and is Corporate maxed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Retail plus SME will stay at 85-88% and Corporate is the balance; it has 'maxed out' on Corporate, with excess originations to be syndicated down.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in PCR across segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Rakesh Bhatia said it reflects Stage-3 ageing mix, moving PCR about 30-40 bps quarter to quarter; ECL grades refreshed quarterly with no material change in TTC PD or LGD.

qa_highlights.question: Capital comfort level and need to raise capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 200-250 bps above CET1 minimums; consolidated D/E guided to 6.2-6.3x, with capital adequate through June-September 2028 on guided book growth.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expense growth of 21% YoY: what is underlying?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth is distorted by the appraisal-cycle change; normalised growth is about 16%. Cost-to-income guided to 33-34% by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds outlook and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds expected up about 8-10 bps for FY27 on a daily-average basis; NIMs targeted up about 10 bps for the year. Floating-rate book is about 70%, with rate changes passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan strategy and state expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Approval expected by year-end; about 500+ branches over 2.5-3 years and INR4,000-5,000 crore portfolio; target states identified but not disclosed, with some in northern India. Acquired entity to be renamed under Tata Capital once a subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon and El Nino impact on rural and vehicle books?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has seen no impact on the portfolio so far and sees no early signs of stress.

risks_watch: Cost of funds rising on incremental borrowing (7.28% vs 7.15% QoQ); management guides +8-10 bps for FY27.
Motor Finance book shrinking QoQ; turnaround to growth expected from Q3 FY27 and ROA target of 2% by FY28.
Rising unsecured book and new gold loan segment; approvals from RBI for Yogloans pending until about year-end.
Macro risks flagged: elevated energy prices, El Nino/monsoon, CPI at 4.38% in June, and possible repo rate hike (management is rate-neutral in guidance).
Credit cost held at about 1% despite new products; Q1 benefited from seasonal benign trend, and management noted that the Q1 credit cost was 'in line with FY28 guidance'.
PCR movements (30-40 bps QoQ) tied to Stage-3 ageing; monitor provisioning trend.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q1 growth, asset quality and operating leverage, with the CEO calling it an 'excellent quarter'. Cautious on macro risks such as energy prices, El Nino and funding costs, and conservative on CV, construction equipment and petro-reliant MSME segments. Evasive on specific gold-loan target states and the timing of Housing Finance listing.
key_quotes: Our asset quality metrics remains resilient, underscoring the strength of our portfolio, underwriting discipline and collections infrastructure.
we expect the gap to narrow over the next 2-3 quarters as sustained origination momentum translates into book expansion.
whatever comes further from credit cost will be a bonus. We are not factoring that in.
we are fairly, I would say, optimistic on meeting our guidance which we have given to the market.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 AUM growth of 23-25% (on track) and FY28 ROA of 2.6% and cost-to-income of 33-34%, backed by Q1 disbursements up 33% YoY to INR46,212 crore, 38% high-margin mix and repricing, plus the Yogloans gold-loan acquisition pending RBI approval; no new capacity build-out quantified beyond 14 branches added in Q1.
